avis.titre: It makes you believe it's working, but it's not
avis.texte: I really wanted this to be the holy grail, so when I first saw it on sale a while back, I actually bought two. It's from a reputable brand, and when you use it you'll see what looks like large amounts of dead skin coming off. In reality, it's the cellulose in the product clumping together. After using it several times since purchasing, I just didn't experience the results everyone seems to rave about. It works fine, but for me it performs about the same as products you can pick up at the drugstore.

Love this product. Removes/dissolves dead and flaky skin. I have used this for years. Especially in the winter months my skin get very dry and looks flaky when i put my make up on. I use this about once a week and my skin is so smooth afterwards.

The only downside is the peeling texture, which some people won't like, and it's probably not for you if you prefer chemical exfoliants. This is a solid exfoliator I keep coming back to because it does what it's supposed to without causing irritation.

I do have extremely dry skin but this prouduct doesn't dry it out too much but I do apply moisturizer religiously after applying this or anytime I wash my face.

avis.titre: go read about cellulose before claiming false advertising!
avis.texte: the post below me claims false advertising because they were lead to believe somewhere that the clumps of cellulose used as a physical exfoliant in this scrub were supposed to be "dead skin balling up and coming off your face" or something. it LITERALLY states "celluloae" as an exfoliating ingredient, and boy does that stuff buff you nice, fine. and gently. along with the chemical exfoliants in this and the glycerin it not only cleans my pores but balances my moisture as well

Guys, that stuff that balls up and comes off is product, NOT your dead skin. Hard core chemical peels dont even make chunks of your skin just fall off your face lol, much less rubbing this around on your skin for a few minutes. Its usually cornstarch or other clumping ingredients in products like this that ball up on your skin, and they tell you its your dead skin magically coming off. No. Its absolutely misleading and the only resason they can make that claim is because rubbing any product on your face technically exfoliates a tiny bit, but these peeling products are not doing anything more than clumping up as you combine the ingredients and then falling off into your hands. Please don't pay almost fifty dollars for something like this. You can get other fabulous exfoliators for that price that actually make a difference.
